resources.title: Housing — Bray
resources.body: Bray 1-bedroom apartments listed at approximately EUR 1,650-2,050 per month on Daft.ie (Sea Gardens EUR 2,050; Meath Road EUR 1,650; Upper Dargle Road EUR 1,600). Bray is a coastal commuter town in Co. Wicklow with DART rail access to Dublin. Deposit norm is typically one to two months rent.

resources.title: Banking — Bray
resources.body: To open a bank account in Ireland, newcomers need photo ID (passport), proof of address (utility bill or tenancy agreement dated within 3 months), and PPS number if employed. AIB and Bank of Ireland both operate in Bray.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Bray
resources.body: No IB or international curriculum schools confirmed via source fetch specifically for Bray. The main national schools directory is via the Department of Education. Families may access Dublin-area international schools given the DART commute proximity.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Bray
resources.body: Non-EU expats staying more than 90 days must register with Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) within 90 days of arrival to obtain an Irish Residence Permit (IRP). Registration is done via the ISD online customer portal. Fee is EUR 300.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Bray
resources.body: A PPS number is obtained by applying online via MyWelfare.ie (if you have a MyGovID account) or by booking an in-person appointment at your local Intreo centre or DSP office. You need photo ID and proof of address.

resources.title: Transport — Bray
resources.body: Bray is served by DART (Dublin Area Rapid Transit) rail and Bus Eireann bus routes. It is in the commuter rail zone for Dublin. Monthly adult TFI Leap Card for Zone 1+2 (covering Bray-Dublin DART corridor) is EUR 129.50. EU/EEA licence holders can exchange at NDLS. Newcomers register with a local GP; medical card via HSE mywelfare.ie.

resources.title: Housing — Navan

resources.title: Housing — Waterford
resources.body: Waterford city centre 1-bedroom apartments listed at approximately EUR 1,300 per month on Daft.ie. Deposit norm is typically one month but up to two months under Irish RPZ rules. Daft.ie is the main local rental portal.

resources.title: Banking — Waterford
resources.body: To open a bank account in Ireland, newcomers need photo ID (passport), proof of address (utility bill or tenancy agreement dated within 3 months), and PPS number if employed. AIB and Bank of Ireland both operate in Waterford.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Waterford
resources.body: Waterford has no IB or French international school listed on the Department of Education school finder. The main schools directory for Ireland is available via the Department of Education. Most international families use the Irish national curriculum schools.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Waterford
resources.body: Non-EU expats staying more than 90 days must register with Immigration Service Delivery (ISD) within 90 days of arrival to obtain an Irish Residence Permit (IRP). Registration is done via the ISD online customer portal booking system. Fee is EUR 300.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Waterford
resources.body: A PPS (Personal Public Service) number is obtained by applying online via MyWelfare.ie (if you have a MyGovID account) or by booking an in-person appointment at your local Intreo centre or DSP office. You need photo ID and proof of address.

resources.title: Transport — Waterford
resources.body: Waterford is served by Bus Eireann city bus services. The adult monthly TFI Leap Card pass for the Waterford City Red Zone is EUR 54. Non-EU licence holders must apply to NDLS to exchange; EU/EEA licences can be exchanged directly at NDLS. Newcomers ordinarily resident in Ireland register with a local GP practice directly; medical card can be applied for via HSE for full eligibility.
